Name: Generation Y
✨ Lightbulbs
Notes:
Track 1 on Generation Y, recorded in 2009. Released as a music video on January 11th, 2011. Description on Bandcamp (March 1st, 2012) reads:

"I can promise you that as I type this right now, 15-year-old kids who have been freaking out over this album are in front of their computers, trying to make their own version of this music. We'll see how that goes. But the impulse makes sense. Lightbulbs, feels like music that comes from inside, as if the act of listening completes it."

Name:
Operation: Kill Hannah Montana
(Operation: Kill Jesus, Hannah Montana)
Notes:
Track 2 on Generation Y, recorded in 2009. Released as a music video on January 15th, 2011. Description on Bandcamp (March 1st, 2012) reads:

"His voice oozes ethereality and sophistication.The instrumentation is graceful and measured. "Operation: Kill Hannah Montana" A haunting number that explicitly deals with a young man's religous suicide. Though notably subdued and tinged with sadness, "OPERATION: KILL HANNAH MONTANA" isn't a downer. You sense an artist known in part for his detachment leaning in close to share a secret."

Name: ✨ Operation: Kill Chet Haze
Notes:
Track 7 on Generation Y. Released as a music video on January 15th, 2011. Description on Bandcamp (March 1st, 2012) reads:

"Every once in a while a record appears out of the ether without clear reference points. Web details on DeVon Hendryx are sketchy, his music is similarly unknowable, in the sense that it's difficult to classify. Despite "Operation: Kill Chet Haze's" unique sound, the record, on one level, is not hard to pin down. What's difficult is conveying how these few everyday pieces are placed together so artfully to create something this striking and unique."

Name:
✨ Generation Y/nilaplliK
(Generation Y, Operation: Kill Palin, nilaplliK)
Notes:
Track 3 on Generation Y, recorded in 2008. Description on Bandcamp (March 1st, 2012) reads:

"Generation Y" isn't a blast of political turmoil. Instead, it's DeVON tuning back into everyday life and micro-level personal relationships. In its brief onslaught of sneery fun, "Generation Y" only occasionally reaches the dizzy pop heights of some contemporary music. But it does give us the rapper DeVon who, seems to be having a blast doing what he's doing. And it's great to learn thas DeVON exist in a world full of smart-phones and stupid people. I'd sigh with relief if the thing hadn't left me breathless."

Name: ⭐️ End To The Means [V1]
Notes:
Track 8 on Generation Y, recorded in 2009. Description on Bandcamp (March 1st, 2012) reads:

"The first time through, hearing "End To The Means" explode into this weird sing-along affair jig is a bit of a shock. Given its fragmented genesis, it's surprising how listenable and of-a-piece "End To The Means" is. It refracts Aquarian optimism through a modern sense of uncertainty, undercutting the loop's jovial lilt with a tricky structure and lyrics that seem confused about what will happen next. It's not easy to take a cut-up voice and make it the centerpiece of a tune, and it's harder still to sing along with it in a way that doesn't sound forced. But "End To The Means" sounds as natural as something that grew out of the earth."

Name: 🏆 Anne Hathaway
Notes:
The biggest Devon Hendryx grail ever. Released to Bandcamp on January 28, 2011 and to YouTube and MySpace around the same time. The song is a freestyle over the song "None of Dem" by Robyn. Removed from Bandcamp sometime between March 1st and October 18th, 2011 and was up on his YouTube channel as late as September 19th, 2013. Enso Sinatra has said he has heard it but does not have it. Description on Bandcamp (March 1st, 2011) reads:

"It's no secret: Nowadays, most mainstream rappers aren't rappers. The majority just throw a few bars together around Christmastime before getting back to their real hustle, whether it be acting, designing clothes, or thinking about how to make Rick Ross the next Biggie Smalls while sitting behind a desk in a sharp suit. It's fitting, then, for Rapper DeVon Hendryx to randomly start rhyming over pop music smash ("None of Dem") originally made by a Swedish pop star (Robyn) trying to pander to a nationwide audience. True, "Anne Hathaway" might come off a bit like a too-perfect couple who drink all night and Farmer's Market all morning, but when they invite you along, saying no kinda makes you an asshole."

There was a possibilty that Anne Hathaway could've been recovered through MySpace, but their databases were erased from their creation to 2019.

When accessing the Anne Hathaway single page, it showed that the download contains two tracks, suggesting that there is a hidden track present. There is no information about what the track could've been, possibly a different version of Anne Hathaway (instrumental, clean version, etc). Nothing else is known about this track.
